newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes higher, aided by crusher buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes higher, aided by crusher buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures finished higher supported by late crusher buying and stronger closes in the CBOT soycomplex, floor traders said.
Earlier, prices had drifted lower amid reports of improved harvest weather in Manitoba and signs the harvest was also picking up in Alberta and Saskatchewan.

Subsequent talk that forecasts suggested another bout of wet weather in western Canada over the weekend renewed concern about harvest delays, with virtually no progress made last week in either Alberta or Saskatchewan.
"It is not at all rosy out west," one oilseed trader said.
Feed grains were lower, amid concern that further wet weather could increase the amount of feed quality grain.
November western barley ended off $0.80 at $145.00, while December feed wheat was down $3.30 at $168.70.
Feed peas and oats remained tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars except for feed peas and oats which are in U.S. dollars).
